grades.quote: On the RISC-V this instruction is amoswap r, a. amoswap reads the value at the memory address a, writes the contents of register r to that address, and puts the value it read into r. That is, it swaps the contents of the register and the addressed memory location. It performs this sequence atomically, using special hardware to prevent any other CPU from using the memory address between the read and the write.
